title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Notation from the previous page: A_r = Chow groups (rational equivalence); A_a = N = cycles modulo algebraic equivalence; A_r^i(X)^a = J^i(X) = algebraically trivial cycles modulo rational equivalence. This page sets out a short chain of hypothetical statements that would make the 'continuous part' of Chow groups behave like Pic^0/Alb, i.e. be abelian varieties.

(1) Hypothesis: on X, the cycles numerically equivalent to 0, taken modulo algebraic equivalence, are described by finitely many algebraic families. Consequences drawn: numerical equivalence would coincide with Matsusaka's tau-equivalence (some multiple algebraically equivalent to 0). The groups A^i_a(X) of cycles mod algebraic equivalence would be finitely generated, generalizing Néron–Severi. A downward arrow (⇓) is attached, perhaps flagging doubt or a further consequence.

(2) Hypothesis: for 0-cycles on X×Y, (x,y)−(x,b)−(a,y)+(a,b) ~ 0. This is trivially algebraically equivalent to 0, so the intended equivalence must be rational. This reading is confirmed by the last line, '2) ⇔ A_0(X×Y)^a ≅ A_0(X)^a × A_0(Y)^a bijective'.

With (1) and (2), Grothendieck expects:
- the A^i_r(X)^a are abelian varieties;
- the exterior product A^i(X)^a × A^j(Y)^a → A^{i+j}(X×Y)^a and the intersection product A^i(X)^a × A^j(X)^a → A^{i+j}(X)^a are morphisms ('est une ...', cut off; presumably bilinear maps/morphisms of abelian varieties);
- for 0-cycles, A_0(X)^a → Alb(X) is bijective (Albanese kernel zero).

The equivalence 2) ⇔ product decomposition is elementary. Write (x,y)−(a,b) = [(x,y)−(x,b)−(a,y)+(a,b)] + [(x,b)−(a,b)] + [(a,y)−(a,b)]. The map (α,β) ↦ α×b + a×β is then surjective iff the bracketed cross term vanishes. It is always injective, via the projections.

The page is thus a programme of 'representability of Chow groups by abelian varieties', presumably meant to feed the standard-conjecture/motives notes around it.
errors: Hypothesis (1) is false in general. Griffiths (1969) found homologically (hence numerically) trivial cycles not algebraically equivalent to zero even modulo torsion, so num ≠ tau-equivalence. Clemens (1983) showed the Griffiths group (hence A^2_a) can be infinitely generated, refuting finite type of A^i_a(X).

Hypothesis (2), taken as rational equivalence, is false. Mumford (1968) proved that for surfaces with p_g>0 (e.g. a product of two curves of positive genus) the Albanese kernel of A_0 is 'infinite dimensional'. So A_0(X×Y)^a ≠ A_0(X)^a × A_0(Y)^a, and A_0(X)^a → Alb(X) is not bijective; the A^i_r(X)^a are not abelian varieties in general.

The relation in 2) is written '~ with a under it' (algebraic equivalence?), under which it is trivially true. The stated equivalence with the product decomposition of A_0(·)^a only makes sense for rational equivalence — a notational slip or ambiguous symbol.

ideas.modern_name: Griffiths group finiteness / num vs tau-equivalence (Matsusaka) / generalized Néron–Severi finite generation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Matsusaka (divisors, 1957); question refuted by Griffiths 1969 and Clemens 1983
ideas.where_published: Related remarks in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) and SGA 6 (num vs tau-equivalence for divisors); exact formulation here unsure

ideas.what: Chow groups of algebraically trivial cycles are abelian varieties, with products given by morphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford 1968 (failure), Roitman, Bloch–Srinivas, Murre (algebraic representative, codim 2)

deep.surprise_reason: A historically interesting snapshot of Grothendieck entertaining the naive 'Chow groups are abelian varieties' programme, close to Mumford's and Griffiths' refutations (1968–69). The mathematics is elementary or known to be false, and there is no uncredited result or unexplored connection.
